_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions) and For Fable (engineering). Items are DELETED when done, never left checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-13 · SkyBridge — Sierra now names the college's own matching courses, C-ID first.
_status: The alignment feature is LIVE (cpl-chat v42) and Sam's ladder is in: Sierra looks first for a course at that college carrying the SAME C-ID as the credit recommendation — the strongest possible match, because C-ID is the statewide course-identity standard, so the equivalence is already established rather than guessed. If there is no C-ID she falls back to matching titles, and only then to a best-judgement wording match, clearly labelled as such. For POST at Cerritos, nine of the ten recommendations now land on exactly one course and six of those are exact C-ID matches; the tenth honestly returns nothing. One line is deliberately flagged: POST lists the same C-ID against two different recommendations, so the match there looks odd and Sierra is told to say so rather than hide it or claim the courses are equivalent. Earlier today she also started reading the full credit-recommendation sets, 38 hidden statewide exhibits came back into view, and the military/non-military split was measured. Next: real testing, with feedback through the Sierra Training tab.

items.text: Re-ask the Cerritos POST question. She should now name AJ 101, AJ 102, AJ 103, AJ 104, AJ 107 and AJ 222 by C-ID rather than telling faculty to go look. The line worth watching is Physical Training and Health Education — POST lists the same C-ID twice, so that match looks odd on purpose and she is told to say so. If the wording there reads badly, that is the first thing to fix.

C-ID coverage is partial (16,067 of 141,696 courses, 112 colleges), so transfer-heavy subjects land on the strong rung while CTE often falls through to the wording match — which was tuned on welding and is weakest there. Do NOT loosen it to catch more, and do not merge the rungs into one score: a wrong-looking suggestion costs more than a missed one.

Try it: pick a college and ask Sierra about a certificate they have not adopted yet — she should name that college's own closest courses AND how other colleges articulated the same thing. The welding example to start with is Cerritos and the FCAW welder qualification. Nobody has read her actual wording yet, so this is the real test.

When a suggestion looks wrong, use the thumbs-down and then 'Write an instruction about this' on the Sierra Training tab. That is how this feature gets corrected — the 25 older untriaged items are now in the way of that, so clearing them is worth an hour.

Split military from non-military wherever a college sees an 'awaiting action' total. Right now the million-plus units is 98.8% military — a service member's transcript brings ~17 recommendations at once, while a certificate brings 1 or 2. Undifferentiated, it reads as an impossible mountain and hides the genuinely achievable part: 10,698 units across 868 students at 28 colleges. Lead with that, then give the military figure with its per-student context. Never present the military bucket as lesser — it all still needs acting on.

The course-catalogue table Sierra searches keeps only the first 900 characters of course titles and 8 sample courses per program. 801 programs are cut off — the biggest ones. So for those, Sierra cannot see most of the courses a college teaches. Worth fixing on its own, separately from the alignment work.

Still open from last session: Sierra says Cerritos has no ironworker CPL when it has a lot. The exhibit list stores the titles as 'FIW Orientation' and 'IW- Mixed Base' — no 'iron' anywhere — while the curated list has 11 rows named 'Ironworker Apprenticeship'. The college-specific search never checks the curated names.

Mission College's CPL coordinator email in MAP is a personal Gmail address (boothmelanie@gmail.com). It is the only one like it across all 123 colleges, and because it is first in the cascade it is what we would propose as the address students get routed to. It is flagged on the tab, not hidden — it is their designation to change, not ours. Worth a word with the MAP team.

7 college contacts are marked 'Candidate — confirm' because we could only find them through a web search, never opening the actual page. Confirming each takes seconds using the links on the tab. Start with Palomar (it has a separate behavioural-health department, so the wrong address is a real risk) and Canyons.

A finding worth a decision: the 36 never-adopted statewide credentials share courses heavily — only 32 distinct courses between them, and 'Introduction to Construction Safety' alone unlocks 12. A college that adds one or two courses could articulate a dozen statewide standards. Want this built as a view colleges can use?

25 pieces of feedback about Sierra have never been triaged — the oldest has been sitting since 1 July. The tab now has buttons to mark each one and to write an instruction about it. This is the single easiest way to make Sierra better.
12 credentials are marked statewide in the adoption file but are missing from Sierra's credential list entirely, so she cannot answer about them at all.

Sierra's exhibit list covers 59 of the 123 colleges, and the college profiles behind it have not been refreshed since 25 June. Any 'no college does this' answer she gives is measured against half the system.

Decision needed before the Finance phrase goes to anyone in Finance: right now a site phrase opens its own tabs PLUS every shared CPL tab. That is fine only if everyone holding it should see all shared CPL data. If not, the scopes need splitting.
The college/district name crosswalk is built and verified but has never been written to the database — that write is what actually ends the 'Mt San Antonio vs Mt. San Antonio' mismatch.
